f_a48e6613516c.answer: No. Growing up is only one part. A life cycle has four parts: born, grow, reproduce (have young) and die. Then the new young start the cycle again.

f_a8e2c8538f1c.question: Why does the last chicken card go back to the first card?
f_a8e2c8538f1c.answer: The hen sits on new eggs. Those eggs hatch into chicks, and the chicks grow up. So the cycle starts again with the new young.

f_c26c1dff1605.question: Why do we draw our bean seed in a journal?
f_c26c1dff1605.answer: Scientists learn by looking closely and writing or drawing what they see. We draw the seed today. We will draw the same seed again as it changes. Sprouts need several days, so today’s page shows only the seed.

f_24653d924f69.question: Is a plant really alive if it doesn’t move?
f_24653d924f69.answer: Yes. Moving is not the test. Living things grow and change, and they need food, water and air. A plant grows and needs water and air, and it makes its own food using sunlight and water. So it is alive even though it stays in one place.

f_9fa4e7f4216c.question: Why is the bean seed in the living group when it just sits there?
f_9fa4e7f4216c.answer: A seed looks still, but it is alive and it will grow into a plant. Our bean gets water from the damp paper towel and air from inside the bag. It uses food stored inside the seed to begin growing. A dry seed is resting, not dead. It wakes up when it gets water.

f_45fbae108401.question: The toy truck moves. Why is it nonliving?
f_45fbae108401.answer: Moving is not enough to make something alive. A toy truck does not grow, and it does not need food, water or air. We ask what a thing does and needs. Since the truck does not grow or need anything, it stays in the nonliving group.

f_9b199619d728.question: Why did the bean get bigger?
f_9b199619d728.answer: The seed took in water. Water from the damp towel makes the seed swell, so a soaked bean is bigger and softer than a dry bean.

f_d2af2c7bf11e.question: What is the first part to come out of the seed?
f_d2af2c7bf11e.answer: The root comes out first. It grows out of the seed and down. After the root, a small shoot pushes up. It will grow into the stem and leaves.

f_e0839ed73e1b.question: My bean has no root yet. Is it dead?
f_e0839ed73e1b.answer: Not necessarily. Every seed grows at its own speed, and some beans show only a tiny root or none yet. It may still be waking up. Keep your bag sealed, draw what you see, write the date, and look again next time.

f_bf7df77b9540.question: Is the flower the seed?
f_bf7df77b9540.answer: No. The flower is not the seed. The flowers on the adult plant make pods, and the pods hold the new bean seeds.

f_5ff0a4ec560b.question: Why do we start with a seed and end with new seeds?
f_5ff0a4ec560b.answer: The new seeds in the pod can be planted. When they are planted, they grow and the life cycle starts again. That is why we order the cards from seed to seed.

f_14dd3f3996fb.question: Which card comes first, the seedling or the adult plant?
f_14dd3f3996fb.answer: The seedling comes first. It is a small plant with its first green leaves. It grows bigger into the adult plant with flowers. If you are not sure, ask which one is bigger.

f_cd146e81a5b1.question: Can we eat the beans?
f_cd146e81a5b1.answer: No. Never eat raw beans or seeds from our lesson. Ask your teacher if you have questions about allergies.

f_76c7fe155e9d.question: Is the caterpillar sleeping inside the chrysalis?
f_76c7fe155e9d.answer: No. It looks still, but a lot is happening inside. The caterpillar’s body changes into a butterfly’s body, with wings, legs, antennae and a long mouth for sipping. This stage is called the pupa.

f_56591286ca26.question: Does the caterpillar turn back into the butterfly’s egg, or does the butterfly turn back into a caterpillar?
f_56591286ca26.answer: No. The butterfly does not turn back into a caterpillar. The adult butterfly lays new eggs on a leaf. A new caterpillar hatches from each new egg, and the cycle starts again.

f_c7347b4006ba.question: How long does a monarch stay in the chrysalis, and what happens when it comes out?
f_c7347b4006ba.answer: A monarch stays in its chrysalis about 10 to 14 days. When the butterfly comes out, its wings are wet and crumpled. It waits for them to dry before it flies.

f_a9c86a06c56c.question: Does the tadpole’s tail fall off?
f_a9c86a06c56c.answer: No. The tail gets shorter and shorter as the tadpole grows, because the body uses it up. A froglet still has a short bit of tail. An adult frog has no tail.

f_e7ceede32a1c.question: How can a froglet breathe air if a tadpole breathes with gills?
f_e7ceede32a1c.answer: As a tadpole changes, it grows lungs inside its body and loses its gills. Lungs are inside, so we cannot see them in the photos. A froglet uses its lungs to breathe air.

f_c5028c4753b9.question: Which legs grow first, and is a froglet an adult yet?
f_c5028c4753b9.answer: The back legs (hind legs) grow first. Then the front legs grow. A froglet has four legs and a short bit of tail, but it is a young frog, not an adult. It grows into an adult frog with no tail, and the adult frog lays the new eggs.

f_7f68b5297d80.question: Is the caterpillar already a butterfly?
f_7f68b5297d80.answer: No. The caterpillar is the larva stage. A butterfly starts as an egg, and the egg hatches into a caterpillar. The caterpillar is still growing and getting ready for the next stage.

f_6e3e9813fc4b.question: Why does the caterpillar eat so much?
f_6e3e9813fc4b.answer: Food gives the caterpillar energy and helps it grow. Its main job is to eat and grow, so it eats leaves almost all the time. In real life, a caterpillar eats leaves, not cake or pie like the caterpillar in the book.

f_595217bd1b5f.question: How does a caterpillar get bigger if its skin does not stretch?
f_595217bd1b5f.answer: It sheds its skin. This is called molting. A monarch caterpillar molts four times as it grows. The old skin comes off and the caterpillar has room to get bigger.

f_07836e7faff3.question: Why do frogs lay their eggs in water?
f_07836e7faff3.answer: A frog egg is soft and covered in clear jelly. It has no hard shell. The egg needs to stay in water, such as a pond. The tadpole that hatches lives in water all the time.

f_e93ca43f747d.question: Is a tadpole a kind of fish?
f_e93ca43f747d.answer: No. A tadpole looks a bit like a fish because it has a tail and lives in water. But a tadpole is a baby frog. It will become a frog later in its life cycle.

f_518b627a33f7.question: How can a tadpole breathe underwater?
f_518b627a33f7.answer: A tadpole breathes with gills. On a newly hatched tadpole you can see feathery gills on the sides of its head. Gills work for a tadpole the way our nose and lungs work for us when we breathe air.

f_50887d3fec3a.question: Why does a tadpole not count as the same as a butterfly’s chrysalis? Don’t they both go in the middle?
f_50887d3fec3a.answer: No. Only things that both animals have go in the middle. A chrysalis belongs only to the butterfly, so it goes in the Butterfly circle. A tadpole with a tail and gills belongs only to the frog, so it goes in the Frog circle. Both animals start as an egg and grow into adults that lay new eggs, so those cards go in the middle.

f_f2fd295bf31a.question: A froglet has a short tail. Does that mean a tail goes in the “Both” circle?
f_f2fd295bf31a.answer: No. Look back at the tadpole card. The tail and gills belong to the frog. A butterfly does not have a tail when it is young, so “tail” goes in the Frog circle.

f_d02da8204633.question: What does “reproduce” mean?
f_d02da8204633.answer: To reproduce means to make new living things of the same kind. An adult bean plant makes seeds. An adult butterfly lays eggs. An adult frog lays eggs.

f_e14f00dddeae.question: Has our bean reproduced or died yet?
f_e14f00dddeae.answer: No, we have not seen that yet. Our bean is still young. It has not grown flowers or pods with new seeds. The bean plant on the picture cards does all four things: it is born, grows, reproduces and dies.

f_13eee7d4097c.question: Can I switch to a different life cycle after I start drawing?
f_13eee7d4097c.answer: You may switch before you start drawing. Once you begin, stay with the cycle you chose so you have time to draw every stage and label it. You can use the picture cards and your word bank strip the whole time.

f_4fe7c463da80.question: What if I do not know how to spell a label?
f_4fe7c463da80.answer: Use the word bank strip and copy the word from it. Readable spelling is fine. Your label just needs to name the stage with the correct word, such as chrysalis or tadpole.

f_f31cfaf02c4b.question: How will my drawing be scored?
f_f31cfaf02c4b.answer: Your teacher looks at two things: are the stages in the right order, and does each stage have the correct label? Each one gets its own level: Excellent, Good, Developing or Beginning. Spelling does not count. Before you hand in your drawing, read the chart and check your own work. Your teacher decides the levels after class.
